title: Leading Big Projects
subtitle: Lead the work through to a shared outcome
summary: Six teams finish their tasks, but the migrated service still fails. Pip reconnects context, scope, logistics, risk, and a shared definition of done. Milestones should expose evidence; delegation gives ownership to the teams doing the work, not every task to Pip.

concepts.title: Context
concepts.body: Pip distributes tickets before explaining the migration. Each team makes choices that conflict at the handoff. Project context supplies the missing picture: the problem, outcome, constraints, stakeholders, and why it matters. Pip brings affected teams and a dependency into the kickoff. With operational constraints visible, colleagues can handle surprises without asking the project lead to decide every detail.

steps.text: Pip shares the problem before distributing tasks.
Include the people who will build and operate the change.
Expose constraints and dependencies that affect local choices.

concepts.title: Definition of done
concepts.body: “Merged,” says one team. “Adopted,” says another. Pip asks what must be true for the migration to be done. A user completing the flow and recovering from failure is stronger evidence than a closed ticket. Deployment, adoption, support ownership, and retiring the old system may all belong in the agreement. Shared acceptance conditions keep workshop teams from stopping at incompatible finish lines.

steps.text: Pip asks what must be true at completion.
Merged code is one intermediate result.
Agree ongoing ownership and old-system retirement.

concepts.title: Milestones
concepts.body: The slide says “milestone Friday,” but nobody knows what it proves. Pip replaces the date-only checkpoint with a real-data handoff between two teams. A milestone should reveal progress, risk, or a usable outcome while the remaining plan can still change. Colleagues use the result to adjust scope and communicate the new route. Checkpoints coordinate learning; they do not make uncertainty disappear from a calendar.

steps.text: Pip turns a milestone into a learning checkpoint.
Use its evidence to adjust the remaining plan.

concepts.title: Delegation
concepts.body: Pip hands over a task, then keeps answering every decision. That is not much ownership. Delegation needs a clear outcome, relevant context, room to decide, support, and an escalation path. Pip agrees checkpoints with the new owner without taking each choice back. The handoff builds capability and makes the project less dependent on one person’s constant availability; it is more than dropping an unclear ticket on another team.

steps.text: Pip transfers ownership, not just a ticket.
Explain the outcome, context, and decision room.
Agree checkpoints, support, and escalation without taking every choice back.

misconceptions.claim: a staff-plus role is mainly about applying a universal formula.
misconceptions.correction: The chapter treats judgment as contextual: identify forces, listen to evidence, and adapt the response to the actual system and people.

misconceptions.claim: A visible activity or artifact proves the work is complete.
misconceptions.correction: Completion requires a useful outcome, shared understanding, and a way to notice whether the decision worked over time.

scenario.title: Lead the handoff
scenario.context: Pip’s migration has six owners, an external dependency, and no shared finish line. The workshop cannot move the launch window.

options.label: Milestone handoffs
options.benefit: The owners share acceptance evidence and surface dependencies early.
options.cost: Teams must prepare evidence and coordinate at checkpoints.
options.consequence: Pip helps the six owners test the integrated handoff before launch; the external dependency becomes a decision, not a surprise.

options.label: Track tasks only
options.benefit: Task progress is easy to count.
options.cost: Closed tickets can hide a broken integrated flow.
options.consequence: Every team reports completion while the user path remains unusable. Late escalation consumes the immovable launch window.

scenario.debrief: Pip checks the shared outcome, not six separate completion claims. Milestones must reveal whether the handoffs work.

quiz.question: Which definition of done is most complete for a migration?
options: Adoption, operations, and old-system retirement are addressed
quiz.explanation: Completion criteria should include the outcome and the responsibilities after delivery.

quiz.question: What should a project milestone provide?
options: Evidence or a usable outcome for the next decision
A guarantee that the rest of the plan will not change
quiz.explanation: Milestones expose progress and risk while changes remain possible.

quiz.question: What distinguishes delegation from simply assigning a task?
options: Ownership comes with context, support, and decision room
The lead stops checking progress entirely
quiz.explanation: A new owner needs enough information and authority to act, plus agreed support.

exercise.title: Make the next move legible
exercise.prompt: Describe a staff-level decision, the people and terrain involved, and the route by which you will learn whether it worked.

fields.label: What is done for the user?
fields.placeholder: Write the concrete facts, people, and constraint.

fields.label: Where should the next handoff occur?
fields.placeholder: State the choice and its trade-off.

fields.label: What evidence belongs at the checkpoint?
fields.placeholder: Name the evidence or conversation that will revisit it.

Merged code is one intermediate result.
Agree ongoing ownership and old-system retirement.
